item.title: Generative Models: Variational Autoencoders and Diffusion Models
item.author: yzj5306@psu.edu (Yiyang Jiang)
item.description:
Presenter Mengyao Zhang (Prof. Binghai Yan’s group, Penn State)
Date September 21, 2026 · 4:30–6:00 PM
Location Davey 339
Topic Stat Mech in Machine Learning — generative models: VAEs and denoising diffusion
Notes Handwritten, 6 pages (viewer and download below)

How do you draw a fresh sample from the distribution of natural images, when the only distributions you can sample directly are the uniform and the Gaussian? Both answers in this session start the same way. Draw a latent variable $z$ from a simple distribution, then learn a map that sends it to data. Training by maximum likelihood then runs into one obstacle: the posterior over the latent variable is intractable. The variational autoencoder handles it with one learned Gaussian posterior and a single decoding step, trained on the evidence lower bound (ELBO) with the reparameterization trick. The denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) has $T$ latent layers, and it fixes the approximate posterior to be a known noising process, so no encoder is learned at all. Its ELBO then collapses to a remarkably simple objective: predict the noise that was added. The handwritten notes carry every derivation, from the Gaussian-mixture M-step, through the closed-form Gaussian KL, to the DDPM posterior mean and sampling loop.

item.title: Neural Networks for Physicists: From One Neuron to Attention
item.author: yzj5306@psu.edu (Yiyang Jiang)
item.description:
Presenter Mu-Yang Chen (Prof. Chao-Xing Liu’s group, Penn State)
Date August 3, 2026 · 4:30–6:00 PM
Location Davey 339
Topic Neural networks for physicists — from one neuron to attention

A three-part pedagogical tour: what a neural network actually is and how it is trained, what attention adds once the data are sequences, and how both are being used right now in many-body physics — neural-network wavefunction ansätze optimised by variational Monte Carlo, and reduced density matrices learned without the wavefunction at all. The organising claim: a network is a very flexible fitting function, and the physics lives entirely in the details of how much of it you build in by hand.
